summary: Polished the TASK-008 character-led GPU proof into a 60s cinematic sequence addressing all 8 problems listed in the task's review. Kept the exact same character identity (assets/character/character_reference_sheet.png, unchanged) and the milestone-1/2/3 engine (motion_graphics.py primitives, create_poc_scene's THEME system) -- no rewrite, only additive fixes: (1) character is now always composited in fixed, bounds-clamped post-camera screen coordinates (safe_character()), so no camera work can ever clip it; (2) character_assets.py locates the true alpha-density valley between each pair of poses instead of splitting the sheet into equal-width columns, which eliminated the adjacent-pose bleed at 3 of 4 pose boundaries at the root cause (verified: left-edge alpha on 'explaining'/'thinking'/'closing' dropped to ~2 out of 255, from 67-94 before); (3/4) every beat now draws inside a shared translucent 'stage' backdrop panel that visually groups the character with its diagram instead of floating both in empty canvas; (5) a new hand_point()/hand_connector() pair draws a connector line from the character's gesturing hand to the diagram it references; (6) motion_graphics.text_reveal() wipes the hook title in left-to-right instead of a static fade; (7) a new motion_graphics.Camera pushes/pans specific diagram coordinates per beat while the character is explicitly excluded from that transform, so camera movement is object-level and intentional rather than a canvas-wide crop; (8) beat boundaries now cross-fade with a real overlap window (the next beat starts fading in before the previous one finishes fading out) plus a brief light sweep, replacing a hard cut that was previously producing a near-blank frame at every transition -- caught and fixed during self-review before the final render, along with a character/diagram-label collision in the PARALLEL beat and a grid/caption overlap in the SCALE beat.
